key_insight: This paper shows that deep learning can estimate cell count and viability directly from brightfield images, removing the need for fluorescent staining. In simple terms, it enables label-free, non-destructive quality checks for cell cultures.
problem_solved: Traditional viability assays rely on dyes that can alter cells, add workflow complexity, and create ambiguity in some cases. The paper addresses the need for a faster, less invasive, and more scalable way to count cells and assess viability.
method: Use brightfield microscopy images as input, instead of stained or labeled samples.
Train a deep learning model to predict cell count and viability from image patterns visible in standard imaging data.
Evaluate the approach as a label-free alternative to conventional staining-based cell viability measurement.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates how computer vision can replace expensive or disruptive lab assays with non-invasive inference from routine images. It is especially relevant for biomanufacturing and drug development workflows where speed, scalability, and sample integrity matter.

paper_title: Label-free cell counting and viability prediction with brightfield imaging and deep learning
paper_authors: Amir Reza Vazifeh, Christian Zeigler, Sornanathan Meyyappan, Richard Jeske, Jason W. Fleischer
